Carbon nanotubes used were multi-walled with particle sizes <8 nm, 30–50 nm, and 48–78 nm.
Polyester resin was used as the polymer matrix with 1% CNT loading.
Radar absorption was measured in the 8–12 GHz frequency range using a Network Analyzer.
XRD confirmed the crystalline structure of the CNTs in the composites.
SEM images showed homogeneous and stable CNT dispersion without additional processing.
VSM analysis revealed that saturation magnetization and coercivity decrease with increasing CNT particle size.
The minimum reflection loss value was −9.38 dB for the 48–78 nm CNT composite.
The effective bandwidth for the best composite was 10.27 GHz.
Radar absorption improved as CNT particle size increased due to enhanced dielectric loss.
CNTs were used without functionalization and had a purity of 96%.
Mechanical mixing for 15 minutes was used to blend CNTs with polyester resin.
Samples were cured for 2 days at room temperature before testing.
The study used a 8720D Network Analyzer and a special mold to ensure sample integrity during measurements.
The composites demonstrated solid absorption, low weight/thickness, and cost-effectiveness.
The research contributes to optimizing microwave absorption properties for future radar absorbing material applications.
Increasing particle size reduces surface-to-volume ratio, affecting magnetic properties.
The study aligns with previous research showing CNT composites' effectiveness in electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding and radar absorption.
The composites were single-layer configurations.
The reflection loss values and absorption bandwidths can be tuned by adjusting CNT particle size.
